classification.difficultyReason: Extend congruence reasoning to quadrilateral pieces, using parallelogram properties to derive equal remaining lengths by subtraction and matching angles through parallel lines and the perpendicular cut.

content.prompt:
If this parallelogram is cut as shown, explain why the two pieces are congruent.
(hint: what are the properties of a parallelogram?)

spec.description: Unshaded parallelogram ABCD with E on AB and F on DC, matching double ticks on AE and FC, a red dashed cut EF, red endpoints and a right-angle square marking angle EFD. Ordinary source blue outlines are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: AB is parallel and equal to DC; AD is parallel and equal to BC; AE = FC; EF is perpendicular to DC. The pieces have corresponding vertex order AEFD and CFEB.
spec.answerVisibility: All geometry and supplied marks remain visible in the student edition; no answer annotations are added.

answer.short: The pieces $AEFD$ and $CFEB$ are congruent: their corresponding sides and angles are equal.
answer.worked:
$AE=FC$ (given), $AD=BC$ (opposite sides of a parallelogram), and $EF$ is common.

Since $AB=DC$ and $AE=FC$,
$$\begin{aligned}EB&=AB-AE\\FD&=DC-FC\\EB&=FD.\end{aligned}$$
Thus all four pairs of corresponding sides are equal.

$\angle ADF=\angle CBE$ and $\angle DAE=\angle BCF$ (opposite angles of a parallelogram).

$\angle EFD=90^\circ$ (marked), so $\angle EFC=90^\circ$ (angles on a straight line). Since $AB\parallel DC$, co-interior angles give $\angle FEA=\angle FEB=90^\circ$.

All corresponding sides and angles of $AEFD$ and $CFEB$ are equal, so the two pieces are congruent.
